documentation.rationale: The identity half is decent. There is a VIN, a clean Carfax with 12 records, a dated Panoz letter tying the chassis to its marketing history and mileage, and the title in hand. The maintenance half is missing: no recommissioning receipts, no detailed underbody photos, no smog evidence.

condition.rationale: The photos show a clean body, interior and engine bay. However, the seller concedes the tires are aged, finish imperfections are disclosed, and the underside shows surface rust and an unexplained residue. After roughly 33 years of mostly sitting, 'mechanically sorted' is undocumented.

price_value.rationale: There is no fair-value estimate or comps. The current $13,000 bid is within the ideal band, but the hammer is unknown. Known tire replacement and a probable recommissioning, plus irreplaceable bespoke parts, temper the value.

mission_fit.rationale: It has a manual, a V8 and plenty of point of view. As a bridge it conflicts with the brief on reliability after storage, unobtainable body and trim parts, uncertain CA registration, and a thin resale market for a 44-car model within 6-24 months.

logistics.rationale: It is in Edmond, OK, and the remote BaT auction closes within about a day. No stated PPI access, and CA smog/registration feasibility is unresolved. BaT shipping and Verified Checkout are available.

ppi_focus: Stainless chassis welds and mounting tabs at the suspension pickups, motor/transmission mounts and cycle-fender brackets.
Galvanic and filiform corrosion where the aluminum panels meet steel fasteners and frame; clamshell hood hinge and latch cracks.
Fuel system: hose age, pump pressure, tank and sender condition, injector function, any fuel smell.
Brake hydraulics: fluid condition, caliper function, original flex hoses.
Cooling: radiator core, fan operation, thermostat, water pump weep; heat soak at idle.
Compression test, idle quality, IAC/TPS/vacuum leaks, EEC-IV codes.
Gearbox tag, synchro behaviour, clutch engagement and hydraulics; LSD chatter and pinion seal.
Source of the underside residue; oil leaks at the rear main, oil pan and valve covers.
Tire date codes; coilover dampers and rod ends.
Emissions equipment and label versus CA smog requirements.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: dated recommissioning invoices plus a clean third-party PPI arranged before the close.
Up: confirmation that the car can pass CA smog and register (emissions label, cats, DMV/BAR answer on the 7,500-mile rule).
Down: a dated Carfax sequence showing a reading below 639 after 2017, or other odometer doubt.
Down: chassis weld cracks, aluminum corrosion, or a fluid leak behind the underside residue.
Down: a hammer price well into the upper budget, given the known tire and recommissioning work.
evidence.mission_note: It meets the manual-and-character part of the enthusiast brief, but it is a collectible stored car with unobtainable body parts, unresolved CA registration and thin resale, so it fits poorly as a reliable, easy-to-resell bridge. It reads more as a keeper-type curiosity than a bridge.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity and provenance well: the VIN matches a photographed 2017 Panoz After Market Sales letter that documents the car's marketing history and 639 miles, and a clean Carfax with 12 records exists. The drivetrain is a visibly Ford 302 HO with a five-speed manual, though the stated T45 gearbox needs tag confirmation. Observed issues are aged tires (conceded by the seller), disclosed finish imperfections, a replaced taillight bezel, and exhaust surface rust and unexplained residue in the single underside photo. The 'mechanically sorted' claim has no receipts behind it on a car that has covered about 695 miles in 33 years. A small mileage sequencing question exists between the Carfax 631 reading and the letter's 639. The largest open items are California smog and registration feasibility for a low-mile Oklahoma car, chassis weld and aluminum corrosion condition, and whether any PPI can happen before a close roughly a day away.
evidence.next_action: Before the close, message the seller for the emissions label and catalytic converter photos, the tire date codes, recommissioning invoices and the dated Carfax odometer entries. In parallel, ask CA DMV/BAR whether a non-CA-certified 1993 vehicle under 7,500 miles can be registered.
